all_found.desc: [ADVISORY] 'unittest real failures' (FAILED (failures=1, expected failures=1)) is caught by the ordinary FAILED/failed pattern alone, so it does not exercise the expectedFailures neutralization from the failing side. A broadened expectedFailures that also swallowed a real 'failures=N' count would not be caught by this case; only the passing-side case pins the helper.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The ~115 cases run in one map-driven loop with no t.Run subtests, so a failure is not isolated or individually runnable (go test -run), and map iteration order is random. When a regex tweak breaks a case, the output is a flat list of Errorf lines, and a single case cannot be rerun.

[ADVISORY] 'unittest real failures' (FAILED (failures=1, expected failures=1)) is caught by the ordinary FAILED/failed pattern alone, so it does not exercise the expectedFailures neutralization from the failing side. [ADVISORY] The doc says the listed exemptions are 'and nothing else', but the code also exempts unittest 'expected failures=N' (expectedFailures), which is not listed. The architecture map understates the exemption set; a maintainer trusting the doc would not know 'OK (expected failures=1)' is neutralized.
